items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: is it Steinberg? The artist? The New Yorker artist that, in a nutshell, there’s nothing west of the Hudson.

ctx.x: I never thought about it because really most of my heroes were players on the east coast, but having said that I mean there were such great players out here I almost hesitate to say — when I say “most” I mean maybe more back there than in L.A. But Hampton Hawes was active and really playing at his peak, and Carl Perkins, another great pianist who also died very young, Russ Freeman, I mean there were wonderful, wonderful players out here. And again as I alluded to earlier, had they gone back east and stayed back…

York. I remember seeing Miles out in L.A. the first time. But you know that whole east coast/west coast thing, by the ‘60s I think it had somewhat subsided. That was more of a journalistic big deal in the ‘50s. And I think it sold a lot of records in both directions and it created kind of a stir, you know there’s nothing like some kind of a real or fictional rivalry to kind of whip things up and get a little more press maybe. But it was very real. I remember the articles that would come out about east coast and…
Oh he did the thing with all New York and in back there’s this teeny little—
